extracted.intended_audience: prospective patent applicants, patent agents, and practitioners using the UK Patent Office under the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act 1883
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and form requirements for making, filing, and prosecuting patent applications (and related proceedings) before the UK Patent Office under the 1883 Act and the Board of Trade Patents Rules. Covers required forms, document formats, notices, hearings, affidavits/declarations, exhibitions, fees, and related jurisdictional savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms substitution and use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Forms A, A1, B, and C in the Second Schedule (to these Rules) shall be used in place of the Forms A, B, and C in the First Schedule to the Act; Forms A and A1 relate to applications, B to provisional specifications, and C to complete specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 5: Forms A, A1, B, C in Second Schedule substituted for earlier forms. See Patents Rules, 5 and Patent Forms references for specific form content and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory application form
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent must be made either in the Form A or the Form A1 set forth in the Second Schedule hereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 6(1): Form A1 is adapted to communicated inventions. The application is in the form of a declaration which can only be made by the applicant himself (see S. 5 sub-s. (2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory provisional and complete specification forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The Form B of provisional specification and the Form C of complete specification shall respectively be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 6(2): Use of these specific forms is required; Form B/ C in Patents Rules replace earlier forms (see Patents Rules, 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Other schedule forms may be used as applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Remaining forms in the Second Schedule may, as far as applicable, be used in any proceedings under these rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 6(3): Use other listed forms where relevant to the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office hours
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Office shall be open to the public every week-day from ten to four, except on specified holidays (Christmas Day, Good Friday, Her Majesty's birthday observance, days observed for public fast/thanksgiving or Bank of England holidays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 7: Office location and misprint note ('and' is misprint for 'to'). See S.98 for Bank-holidays at present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent must be signed by the applicant, but other communications and attendances may be made by or through an agent duly authorised to the satisfaction of the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 8: The application declaration can only be made by the applicant himself; agents may act for other communications and may be required to be resident in the United Kingdom if the Comptroller so requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent authorisation and residence
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents acting for applicants must be duly authorised to the satisfaction of the Comptroller and, if required by him, resident in the United Kingdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 8: Applies to communications and attendances before the Comptroller; authorisation must satisfy the Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of address mandatory and binding
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall be accompanied by a statement of an address to which all notices, requisitions, and communications may be made; such statement is binding upon the applicant until a substituted statement is furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 9: The Comptroller may in any particular case require that the address be in the United Kingdom. Fee for altering address is specified in the First Schedule to these Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document language, format, and legibility
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents and copies furnished to the Comptroller or Board of Trade must be written or printed in large and legible characters in the English language upon strong wide-ruled paper (one side only), size 13 inches by 8 inches, leaving a margin of two inches on the left-hand side; signatures must be large and legible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 10: Duplicate documents shall be left if required by the Comptroller. This rule prescribes physical and legibility standards for filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller to give notice before adverse discretionary acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Before exercising any discretionary power given to the Comptroller adversely to an applicant (for a patent or for amendment of a specification), the Comptroller shall give ten days' notice, or longer as he thinks fit, to the applicant of the time when he may be heard personally or by his agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 11: See S.94 for statutory basis. Notice period may be extended at Comptroller's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's duty to notify intent to be heard
rubrics_metrics.description: Within five days from the date when such notice is delivered in the ordinary course of post (or such longer time as the Comptroller appoints), the applicant shall notify the Comptroller whether or not he intends to be heard on the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 12: If applicant does not receive notice he will be made aware of it upon receiving notice under Rule 14. For form of notice see Patent Forms, E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller may require written or oral explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether or not the applicant desires to be heard, the Comptroller may require the applicant to submit a written statement within a notified time, or to attend and make oral explanations with respect to matters the Comptroller may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 13: Applies to matters the Comptroller may in each case require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Comptroller's decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision or determination of the Comptroller in exercise of any such discretionary power shall be notified by him to the applicant and any other person affected thereby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 14: Persons affected may include another applicant for the same invention (see note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'applicant' for notice/hearing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'applicant' in Rules 11, 12, and 13 includes an applicant whose specification bears the same as or similar title to that of a prior applicant and has been reported on by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 15: This definition captures contested or overlapping-title situations; see S.7 for statutory reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior and subsequent applicant hearing rights and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior and second applicants may attend hearing of the question whether the inventions in both applications are the same, but neither party shall be at liberty to inspect the specification of the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 16: As to rights of prior and subsequent applicants see S.7 sub-s. (5). Attendance is allowed but inspection of the other's specification is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial/international exhibition temporary use procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person desiring to exhibit an invention at an industrial or international exhibition, or to publish or use the invention during the exhibition, must obtain from the Board of Trade a certificate that the exhibition is industrial or international and give the Comptroller seven days' notice of intention to exhibit, publish, or use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 17: For identification in the event of a later patent application the applicant shall furnish a brief description accompanied, if necessary, by drawings and such other information as the Comptroller may require. See S.57 for Board of Trade certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to amend documents and correct irregularities
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document for which no special provision is made by the Act may be amended, and any irregularity in procedure which the Comptroller deems obviable without detriment to any person's interests may be corrected on such terms as the Comptroller thinks fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 18: The Comptroller has discretionary remedial authority; note commentary that it is doubtful this authorizes amendment of Letters Patent themselves (see notes to S.S. 18, 91).

rubrics_metrics.name: Postal filing deemed delivery rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application, notice, or other document authorized or required to be left, made, or given at the Patent Office or to the Comptroller may be sent by prepaid letter through the post and, if so sent, shall be deemed to have been left, made, or given at the time when the letter containing it would be delivered in the ordinary course of post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 19: In proving such service it is sufficient to show the letter was properly addressed and put into the post. This rule forms S.97 of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits — acceptable officiants and jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits (except where otherwise prescribed) may be used as evidence when sworn: (1) in the UK before any person authorized to administer oaths in the Supreme Court of Judicature or before a justice of the peace for the county/place where sworn; (2) in British dominions outside the UK before any court, judge, justice of the peace, or person authorized to administer oaths there; (3) out of the British dominions before a British minister, consul/vice-consul, person exercising functions of a British minister/consul, a notary public, or a judge/magistrate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 20: See Instructions and case law notes; affidavits may also be taken before a notary per L.T. Feb. 9th, 1884 note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overseas statutory declaration form modification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any statutory declaration prescribed by these Rules is made out of the United Kingdom, the words 'and by virtue of the Statutory Declarations Act, 1835' must be omitted, and the declaration shall (unless context otherwise requires) be made in the manner prescribed in Rule 20(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 21: See also note to Patent Forms A, A1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of recording applications (postal and in-person)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for a patent sent by prepaid letter shall, as far as practicable, be opened and numbered in the order in which the letters containing them have been delivered in the ordinary course of post. Applications left at the Patent Office otherwise than through the post shall be numbered in the order of their receipt at the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 22: Prescribes priority/numbering order for postal and hand-delivered applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees under the Act and Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees to be paid under the Act in addition to the fees mentioned in the Second Schedule thereto, so far as it relates to patents, shall be those specified in the list of fees in the First Schedule to these Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 4: See the First Schedule to the Rules for detailed fee amounts and the Second Schedule to the Act for statutory fees. For form for certificate of payment or renewal see Patent Forms, J.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of former registers
rubrics_metrics.description: The registers of patents and of proprietors kept under any enactment repealed by this Act shall respectively be deemed parts of the same book as the register of patents kept under this Act; similarly for registers of designs and trade marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sect. 114: Transitional provision preserving continuity of former registers; affects how prior entries are treated under the new Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving for jurisdiction of Scotland, Ireland, Isle of Man courts
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions conferring special jurisdiction on the Court under this Act shall not (except as to jurisdiction as expressly extended) affect the jurisdiction of any Court in Scotland, Ireland, or the Isle of Man in proceedings relating to patents, designs, or trade marks; definitions of 'the Court' and 'Court of Appeal' vary by jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sect. 111 and 112: Reserve jurisdiction to local courts; rectification orders from local courts must be served on the Comptroller who shall rectify the register accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation proceedings in Scotland
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings in Scotland for revocation (of a patent) shall be in the form of an action of reduction at the instance of the Lord Advocate or at the instance of a party having interest with his concurrence, which concurrence may be given on just cause shown only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sect. 109(1-2): Service of writs and summonses shall be made according to forms and practice existing at commencement of Act; see Mackay's Court of Session Practice references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scotland — forms of infringement action and summary prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: In Scotland an action for infringement usually takes the form of an action of suspension and interdict, or an action for damages; any offence under this Act declared punishable on summary conviction may be prosecuted in the Sheriff Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sect. 108 and accompanying notes: See Mackay's Court of Session Practice and Bell's Commentaries for procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isle of Man provisions (extension and penalties)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act extends to the Isle of Man, but does not affect the jurisdiction of Isle of Man courts in proceedings for infringement or other patent/design/trade mark matters; the punishment for a misdemeanor under the Act in the Isle of Man may be imprisonment up to two years with or without hard labour and with or without a fine up to £100, at the Court’s discretion, and summary offences may be prosecuted as in England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sect. 112: Contains procedure for prosecution and recovery of fines in Isle of Man; see Patents Rules, Trade Marks Rules, Designs Rules cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal without prejudice (transitional protections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enactments described in the Third Schedule are repealed but the repeal shall not (a) affect past operation or rights acquired under those enactments, (b) interfere with institution or prosecution of actions that may be carried on as if this Act had not been passed, or (c) take away or abridge protections or benefits related to such actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sect. 113: Transitional saving for past acts, pending applications, rights, appointments, compensations, orders, liabilities, and ongoing proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rules made under repealed enactments continued subject to Board of Trade powers
rubrics_metrics.description: All general rules made by the Lord Chancellor or other authority under any enactment repealed by this Act and in force at commencement may be repealed, altered, or amended by the Board of Trade as if they had been made by the Board under this Act, but no such change shall take effect before commencement of this Act; subject to that, such general rules continue in force so far as consistent with and not superseded by this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sect. 115: Preserves existing secondary rules but vests amendment power in Board of Trade. See Patents Rules, 78; Designs Rules, 37; Trade Marks Rules, 60 references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving for Crown prerogative over letters patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Act shall take away, abridge, or prejudicially affect the prerogative of the Crown in relation to the granting of any letters patent or to the withholding of a grant thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sect. 116: Crown prerogative preserved despite statutory framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to application of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: General definitions: 'Person' includes a body corporate; 'The Court' means (subject to Scotland/Ireland/Isle of Man provisions) Her Majesty's High Court of Justice in England; 'Law officer' means the Attorney-General or Solicitor-General for England; 'Treasury', 'Comptroller', 'prescribed', 'British possession', 'legislature', and the meaning of 'summary conviction' in Ireland are defined in S.117 and related notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sect. 117 and following: These definitions determine interpretation of the Act and Rules across jurisdictions and procedural rules; cross-references given for Scotland/Ireland/Isle of Man.
